output.reason: The description reads like a template filled in section by section: what the code does now, what RVSec flagged, the change and why, the effect on users, compatibility, build and test status, and what reviewers should check. Each point gets one short, plain sentence. A multi-step pipeline would likely produce text in this shape. A Claude agent would more likely use headers or bullet points and write more, so SP2 seems less likely. Codex in a single session (TP) usually writes more casually and less evenly. The diff is small and tidy, so it gives little to go on, and this guess is not much better than chance.
